verdict.rationale: Scoped API credentials are a fair question for a financial-data API platform, so the axis applies. The evidence only shows that Teller issues mTLS client certificates to authenticate the API caller, and that end-users grant an application access to their accounts. Nothing documents issuing scoped, least-privilege, or per-agent credentials (e.g., read-only versus payments, or per-endpoint restrictions), and the end-user authorization is an adjacent feature that earns no credit.
